name: 唐揚げ (Karaage) · Japanese Fried Chicken with Kewpie Mayo
englishName: Japanese Fried Chicken with Kewpie Mayo
description: Skin-on chicken thighs marinated in soy, sake, ginger and garlic, coated in potato starch and double-fried for a thin, shattering crust and juicy middle. Served with lemon and Kewpie. Serves 4.

ingredients.text: 600 g boneless skin-on chicken thighs, cut into 5 cm pieces
ingredients.item: boneless skin-on chicken thighs, cut into 5 cm pieces

steps.text: Mix 600 g boneless skin-on chicken thighs, cut into 5 cm pieces with 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp sake, 2 tsp grated ginger, 1 garlic clove, grated, 1/2 tsp sesame oil and 1/2 tsp sugar. Marinate in the fridge for 30 minutes (up to 2 hours).
Heat 1 L neutral oil (for frying) to 160°C. Drain the chicken and toss in 60 g potato starch (katakuriko) until each piece is fully coated, squeezing the starch on so the pieces hold a craggy shape.
Fry in batches for 3 minutes, until pale and just cooked. Lift onto a rack and rest 4 minutes.
Raise the oil to 190°C and fry again for 1 minute, until deep golden and crisp. Drain on the rack.
Serve hot with 150 g green cabbage, finely shredded, 1/2 lemon, cut into wedges and 4 tbsp Kewpie mayonnaise, with shichimi togarashi, to serve sprinkled over the mayo if you like.

notes: Potato starch fries lighter and crisper than flour or cornstarch. The rest between fries lets residual heat finish the inside gently, so the second fry only has to crisp. Skin-on thigh is essential; breast dries out.
